paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. David wanted to do something good for God, and God said, "You are not the one to build Me a house in which to dwell." (1 Chronicles 17:4) Then God flipped the whole thing: "the LORD will build a house for you." (1 Chronicles 17:10) Even our best offerings can't out-give Him, because He is always the one giving first.

Notice how God starts His answer. He reminds David, "I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel." (1 Chronicles 17:7) Everything David had, God handed him. God also promises that David's son will have a throne that lasts forever, and says, "I will be his Father, and he will be My son." (1 Chronicles 17:12-13) I bet that's why we don't have to earn our place with God. He builds the place Himself.

So what does a baker do with a gift like that? Do what David does: sit before the LORD, say "Who am I?", and then say thank You and ask Him to do as He promised. (1 Chronicles 17:16, 23) David even says the promise gave him the courage to pray. (1 Chronicles 17:25) When God hands you the WHOLE bakery, friend, you don't haggle. You just say YES, please!
